 This appeal coming on for hearing this day, the Court   following:
 -------------------------------------------------------------
 ORDER This Misc. Appeal u/S.173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed against the award dated 23.04.2009 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.72/2008 whereby, the claim case filed by claimants was dismissed.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts in brief to decide the appeal are that a claim petition was filed by the claimants for grant of compensation on account of death of Chhotu @ Laxman in a motor accident occurred on 11.06.2007 involving a Bus bearing registration No.MP-08-F-9971 which was being driven by respondent no.1 - Mahendra Arya and was owned by respondent no.2- Anil Sagar.
Respondents No.1 & 2/non-applicant no.1 & 2 - Driver and Owner of the offending vehicle did not appear before learned claims tribunal and were proceeded ex-parte.

Respondent No. 3 - Insurance Company filed its written statement and denied the averments made in the claim petition and further stated that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was being plied in breach of policy terms and conditions because the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident, therefore, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Learned Claims Tribunal framed as many as seven issues and directed both the parties to lead their evidence.
Learned Claims Tribunal after recording of evidence of both the parties dismissed the claim petition.

Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the order impugned passed by the Claims Tribunal is against the settled principles of law as well as material available on record, therefore, the same is liable to be set-aside.
It is further argued that learned Claims Tribunal erred in dismissing the claim only on the ground of non filing of copy of charge- sheet.

Further submission is that learned Claims Smt.Nirmala vs Mahendra Arya on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123656155/
2
Tribunal has also erred in disbelieving the eye-witness merely on the ground that his name is not in the witness-list of criminal case.
The aforesaid findings are against the settled principles of law in claim case and the evidence adduced by claimants are to be seen.

It is further argued that learned Claims Tribunal has also wrongly held that appellants/claimants are not the legal representatives of the deceased, therefore, impugned award be set aside and claimants be awarded appropriate compensation.

On the other hand, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company argued that learned Claims Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition because it is not proved that the deceased was traveling in bus which was met with the accident.
Further argument is that it is also not proved that appellants/claimants are legal representatives of deceased Chhotu @ Laxman.
Hence, present appeal deserves to be dismissed having no merits.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Claimant Smt. Nirmla has examined herself as (AW-1) and proved the documents (Exh.P/1) First Information Report,
(Exh.P/2) Merg Intimation, (Exh.P/3) Last Panchyatnama & (Exh.P/4) Post Mortem Report of deceased Chhotu @ Laxman Rao Rane.

Claimants has also examined (AW-2) Vijay Kumar as an eye- witness and according to this witness,
on 11.06.2007 he was traveling in bus bearing registration No.MP-08-F-9971 at cleaner side and coming to Indore from Bombay.

When the bus reached near Taaiyab Dhaba, Nagalbadi, District Badwani, the bus overtook a truck and hit a standing truck near Dhaba on account of that accident,
Chhotu @ Laxman who was sitting at cleaner side, his body was crushed and he died on the spot.

Learned Claims Tribunal disbelieved the statement of this witness to the details of accident on the ground that his statement was not recorded by the concerned Police in criminal case registered against the driver of bus and the claimants have failed to file the copy of charge- sheet.

However, the above reasons for disbelieving the evidence is not in accordance with settled principles of law in the light of the decision of Apex Court in the case of Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and Anr. [MACD 2019(1) (SC) 42] and held that merely on the ground that name of witness is not shown in the witness list of Criminal Case is not a ground to disbelieve his evidence.

entities.text: Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and Anr. [MACD 2019(1) (SC) 42]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Witness not named in a criminal case, can be examined in claim case.
Respondent has not produced any witness in evidence, therefore, the evidence of the witness was relied upon.
Similarly, in the case of Kusum Lata and Ors. Vs. Satbir and Ors.

entities.text: Kusum Lata and Ors. Vs. Satbir and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [(2011) ACJ 926] the Apex Court held that brother of the deceased lodged FIR but neither number of vehicle nor name of driver was mentioned in it.
Only on this ground, the evidence of eye-witness cannot be discarded.

The Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Lallo Ram Vs. Ram Babu Kamariya and others [(2005) ACJ 1755] held that claim petition cannot be dismissed for not filing of FIR, Challan Papers and documents pertaining to criminal case.

entities.text: Lallo Ram Vs. Ram Babu Kamariya and others [(2005) ACJ 1755]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the findings of Claims Tribunal in disbelieving the statement of (AW-2) eye-witness Vijay Kumar is against the settled principles of law.

3
In the case at hand, as discussed above, the FIR bearing crime no.118/2007 was registered against the driver of Bus bearing registration No. MP-08-F-9971 for causing this accident.
As per Merg Intimation Exh.P/2, the death of Chhotu @ Laxman was investigated and notice was given as per Exh.P/2.
Naksha Panchayatnama of Chhotu @ Laxman was prepared as per Exh.P/3.
Post mortem report Exh.P/4 reveals that death of Chhotu @ Laxman was on account of road traffic accident.
Thus, it is found that Chhotu @ Laxman died in this road accident.

Respondents No.1 & 2/non-applicant no.1 & 2 - Driver and Owner of the offending vehicle remain ex-parte before the Tribunal and Respondent no.3/Insurance Company has not adduced any evidence in rebuttal, therefore, the fact that deceased Chhotu @ Laxman died on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bus bearing registration No. MP-08-F-9971 is also found to be proved.
In this case, the claim petition was filed by Nirmala w/o Narsingh Rao and Narsingh Rao S/o Kishan Rao claiming themselves to be legal representatives (parents) of deceased Chhotu @ Laxman.
Narsingh Rao S/o Kishan Rao has not been examined who is said to be the father of deceased.
(AW-1) Smt. Nirmala in her statements at Para 3 & 4 stated that she had only a son who died in accident.
She and her husband live in Sangle Ka Bada, Taraganj, Lashkar, Gwalior (M.P.).
No one in their family lives in Bina, District Sagar (M.P.).
She has failed to explain that in Merg Intimation (Exh.P/3) and Post mortem Report (Exh.P/4) how the address of deceased is recorded as West Railway Colony, 149 Bina District Sagar (M.P.).
(AW-1) Nirmala admitted that she is having Voter Card and Ration Card, however, she expressed her inability to show the aforesaid documents.
She failed to give answer where the documents are kept.

Even after granting opportunity for evidence,
she has not produced any documents i.e. Voter Card and Ration Card to show that deceased was her son and she is residing at Sangle Ka Bada, Taraganj, Lashkar, Gwalior (M.P.).
In these circumstances, learned Claims Tribunal has rightly held that claimants are not legal representatives of deceased Chhotu @ Laxman.
So far as amount of compensation is concerned, as per Post mortem Report (Exh.P/4), the deceased was 24 year old at the time of accident.

As per claimant Smt. Nirmala, her son was skilled mansion and he was earning Rs.6,000/- per month but she has failed to produce any documents to corroborate the abovesaid facts about the income of deceased; therefore, considering the deceased to be an unskilled labour, his monthly income is assessed as Rs.3,000/- per month.

In the light of the case law of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.; 2017 ACJ 2700 as well as Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors.; AIR 2009 SC 3104,considering the annual income of the deceased to be Rs.36,000/-, dependency 1/2 (Rs.36000x1/2=18,000), future prospect @ 40% (18000 x 40/100=7200), multiplier of 18 [(18000+7200) x 18=Rs.4,53,600/-) and Rs.70,000/- in other heads, total compensation amount comes to Rs.5,23,600/-.
